steps.text: Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C).

Beat butter in a large bowl with an electric mixer until light and fluffy. Add flour, confectioners' sugar, and cornstarch; beat on low for 1 minute, then high for 3 to 4 minutes. Drop spoonfuls of dough 2 inches apart onto ungreased cookie sheets.
Bake in the preheated oven until edges are golden, 12 to 15 minutes. Cool on the baking sheets briefly before removing to a wire rack to cool completely.

raw_recipe.headline: Melt-in-Your-Mouth Shortbread
raw_recipe.description: This is the best shortbread recipe ever, and it's so easy to make with 4 simple pantry ingredients that combine to make a decadent, buttery treat.

review.reviewBody:
I confess I had my doubts when I saw the cornstarch in the recipe. In my mind, shortbread contains butter, flour and sugar in the proper proportions.

However, the good reviews associated with recipe convinced me to try it.

I don't write reviews for recipes because, hey, they're only recipes, right? Let me tell you that this cookie recipe is shockingly good. All the reviews are right-- this is a shortbread with a completely unique presentation and taste. Try it, follow the recipe exactly, and your cookies will rock.

UPDATE 11/27/2002. Made them again, and they are still quite fine. Correct temperature is 350 degrees F, however, and cooking time is 9 minutes. Watch the edges REALLY CAREFULLY because they burn suddenly.

Some reviews claim this recipe can be powdery. That is true IF you eat these cookies hot. For some reason these cookies taste a little better the day after.

If you want people to think you fussed, drop the dough from an icing bag onto your ungreased cookie sheet, through a large star icing tip.

These are definitely melt in your mouth. They were just what I remembered. One thing to keep in mind. They move off the pan easier when they are almost to completely cool. they tend to fall apart if moved before cool.

When I made this recipe as stated, I would've only given it 2 stars. However, after my 2nd batch and the following changes, I give this 5 stars. 
I whipped the butter on high for 10 - 15 minutes, then added the flour, cornstarch, 3/4 cups of powdered (icing) sugar, a slpash of vanilla extract and 3 tbsp of white sugar. I beat that on high for 5 - 10 mins. 
I baked this on a parchment lined baking sheet at 350°f for 8 minutes. That was the perfect temperature and time. The bottoms were just starting to brown, and they continued to cook while on the cooling rack. Turned out delicious! Will make again for sure!

These are spectacular! Whipped butter alone first for about 15 min. Then added powdered sugar plus one extra tbsp powdered sugar. Whipped again 1 min. Added corn starch whipped again 1 min. Added 1/2 c. flour whipped again 1 min. Added 1/2 c. flour and whipped then added the last 1/2 c. flour and whipped again. Put batter in a icing piper used the star tip. baked at 375 for 5 min then switched racks baked for another 5. Then switched again baking at 2 min intervals switch as it goes until beautifully golden. let cool and devour!

I make this every year and they are always a hit. It’s good with either salted or unsalted butter. It’s 50/50 split in my family preference on the butter. I recommend to make a batch with each salted and unsalted then decide. I use a 1M Wilton tip for piping. Make sure to whip for at least 7 mins on high so piping is a breeze. I use parchment paper when baking so the cookies slide easily onto cooling rack.

This will be my new go to recipe for shortbread cookies. It's very similar to my mom's recipe, but the quantities are different. I added and extra 1/8 cup of confectioners sugar as the batter needed a touch of sweetness. I used a small cookie scoop and ended up having to bake (350) them about 12 minutes until they were set and lightly browned around the edges. They are delicious. I used sprinkles on top prior to baking them.

Super easy to make and they really are melt in your mouth. Super tender cookies. Let them cool completely before trying to pick them up or the will crumble. Once cool they are fine. 

I decorated some with colored sugar, some with chocolate drizzle and coated some in powdered sugar. The powdered sugar remind me of the most delicate Mexican wedding cookie you ever had.

The only thing I changed was added 1tsp of vanilla. 350 at 9-10 minutes worked for me. I kind of used the parchment paper to flip a cookie on its side to check doneness. Took them off when they were JUST starting to turn golden and let them sit on the pan for a couple of minutes before transferring to a wire rack.

My son loves whipped shortbread so I decided to add this recipe to my Christmas cookie list. I used homemade vanilla sugar that I ground in the food processor for the icing sugar and added 1/4 tsp salt as I use unsalted butter. This recipe yielded 32 cookies using my #2070 scoop, I baked at 350 for 14 minutes, turning pans halfway through, I used 4 of each red and green glace cherries quartered to decorate the tops. Thanks!

I think this is a fast and simple recipe. I do add a little twist by adding a lemon zest into the batter, then using some of the lemon juice to make a royal icing to drizzel. These cookies melt in your mouth.
I have now made these twice. I used the tips QueenJeanna provided and they turn out perfectly every time. I will definitely make these over & over!

I’ve made these a few times and it makes a big difference to beat the softened butter for about 20 minutes. They are lighter and full of a buttery taste. Those that like shortbread cookies love this recipe.. I make buttercream icing to top off them off. It adds just the right amount of sweetness.
I have not baked for decades. Started in the last month. This recipe is perfection. I did two dozen and they turned out spectacularly.
It really is the beat shortbread recipe ever
These really did melt in your mouth. The texture was weird, but the taste was great! I’d use regular sugar next time.
These are yummy and extremely easy. I add a teaspoon of vanilla extract while whipping the butter and cherries or sanding sugar on top before baking.
I absolutely love this recipe. So quick to make and so delicious too. Looking forward to giving these out over Christmas.
Followed recipe. Very melt in your mouth! Just what I was looking for!! Keeper!!
Beautiful shortbread recipe, no fail directions! Everyone loved them!!
Family loves, very easy to make.
